lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday's Town Council work session, where staff will dig into Comprehensive Plan goals with project consultants, get a Gondola Subcommittee update, and — most notably — review proposals for a third-party audit of the Town's rental housing policies, a question that cuts right to the heart of who can afford to live here. Ouray County's Planning Commission meets virtually Wednesday to work through possible changes to its Land Use Code definitions, which is the quiet upstream work that shapes everything that comes after. Mountain Village's Design Review Board takes up a conditional-use permit for a temporary tent and food truck at 332 Adams Ranch Rd on Thursday.

notable.stake: Third-party rental housing audit review and Comprehensive Plan goals up for discussion.
Land Use Code definition changes debated — shapes future development rules countywide.
Conditional-use permit for tent and food truck at Adams Ranch Rd goes to DRB.
